audit.whatIsWrong: The entry has Danger Zone and Overheat backwards, and builds its level-6 advice on the mistake. spikes[1] says "don't blow it while he's at the silenced danger bar; bait the overheated Flamespitter (Q) first". mid says "if you commit while he's at the danger bar, the overheated free-cast Flamespitter ... eat[s] your health back through the suppress". early says "an overheated Flamespitter shreds you outright". wants.foe[0] has him "hit the overheat danger bar and free-cast an empowered Flamespitter". whys[3] and wants.you[0] both say to burst him "before he can overheat".
audit.why: Riot's Junkyard Titan text: "When he reaches 50% Heat he reaches Danger Zone, granting all his basic abilities bonus effects. When he reaches 100% Heat, he starts Overheating, gaining bonus Attack Speed and granting his basic attacks bonus damage, but making him unable to cast spells for a few seconds." Overheat is the opposite of a free-cast window — it is a self-silence. There is no such thing as an overheated Flamespitter. So the entry tells the reader to refuse the fight in Rumble's weakest window and to hurry the all-in before it arrives, which inverts the single most important timing in the lane. The correct rule is: refuse at 50-99% heat, commit at 100%.
audit.corrected: Danger Zone (50%, empowered abilities) and Overheat (100%, cannot cast) separated and given their real consequences across spikes[1], spikes[3], early, mid, wants.you[0], wants.foe[0], whys[4], breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0], dontsFull[0] and report[5]. Overheat restated as the commit window.

audit.whatIsWrong: "Medarda Maxim" is used as the name of Ambessa's empowered-auto passive in spikes[0], early and wants.you[1]. It is not an ability. Six occurrences of the string exist in champ-data/content/ambessa.js.
audit.why: Ambessa has exactly one passive and it is Drakehound's Step. "Medarda" is her surname; "Medarda Maxim" is not in Riot's data at all. The packet's suspectNames did not flag it because there is no real ability name close enough for the distance check to match.
audit.corrected: Replaced with Drakehound's Step in the three strings in this matchup. The other three occurrences are in matchups outside this slice — flagged in notes.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ambessa.json (P: Drakehound's Step, the only passive)

audit.whatIsWrong: Five strings credit Public Execution with a "flat armor-pen passive" and "heal-on-ability-damage" — spikes[1], mid, late, whys[3] and whys[5], with wants.you[0] adding "burst with your armor-pen passive". whys[5] is built entirely on it: "Your R passive heals on every ability hit, so you out-sustain his point-blank heat DPS".
audit.why: Riot's Public Execution text contains no penetration and no healing: it blinks to the farthest enemy champion in a line, suppresses on arrival, then slams for damage and a stun. Against Rumble this is not a harmless embellishment — the entry is telling the reader they can out-sustain three seconds of Flamespitter through a heal that does not exist, which is exactly the fight that kills them.
audit.corrected: Removed everywhere I touched; the crash stun and the Repudiation brace substituted as the real reasons the all-in converts. whys[5] rebuilt around the Eclipse spike instead.

audit.whatIsWrong: Electro Harpoon's magic resist shred is never mentioned, while dosFull[1] is titled "Build MR" with a description about weaving dashes.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Rumble launches a harpoon, electrocuting his target with magic damage, slowing their Move Speed, and reducing their Magic Resist. Rumble can carry 2 harpoons at a time." Two charges at 850 range that shred MR is the reason the MR you bought is worth less than the tooltip implies, and it is why the recommendation needs to be "more than you think" rather than a single item.
audit.corrected: Written into dosFull[1], late and report[5].

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer's entire win condition is "Track Scrap Shield before every commit" — it is the tldr, the winCon, the focus, dosFull[0], breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.trading and report[5].
audit.why: Scrap Shield's cooldown is a flat 6 seconds at every rank. It is never meaningfully down, so an instruction to wait for it is an instruction never to fight. The cooldown that actually gates this matchup is Flamespitter at 10/9/8/7/6 and, above everything, the heat bar — which is not a cooldown at all but behaves like one. The Equalizer is 130/105/80.
audit.corrected: tldr, winCon, focus.text, dosFull[0], breakdown.cooldowns, phases[1].why and report[5] repointed from Scrap Shield to the heat bar, with the real numbers attached.

audit.whatIsWrong: The whys[] array is off by one stage from level 4 onward. whys[3] sits under "Levels 4-5" but describes Public Execution, which does not exist until 6; whys[4] sits under "Level 6" but describes the Eclipse first-item spike; whys[5] sits under "First item" but describes late-game sustain. phases[1].why also repeats the "Dash-resets stack your passive shield" error found across this champion.
audit.why: A reader at level 4 is told to use an ultimate they will not have for two more levels, and a reader at 6 is told their spike is an item they have not bought. The stages have real content available: 4-5 is where Lacerate reaches 11s and the Repudiation brace starts beating a 3-second cone, 6 is Public Execution, and first item is Eclipse plus Q max.
audit.corrected: whys[3], whys[4] and whys[5] shifted back onto their own stages; phases[1].why corrected.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives Rumble levels 2, 3, first item and two-plus items and rates the lane EVEN at 6/10, on a 53.31% win rate over 302 games, against a champion the same entry describes as having "no dash and no scaling escape".
audit.why: The already-audited mirror file audits/top/rumble__ambessa.json independently reached the same conclusion from Rumble's side and set that page to HARD 7/10 with the chart Rumble, Rumble, Skill, Ambessa, Ambessa, Ambessa, Ambessa — matching the packet levelChart here exactly. Both pages must say the same thing, and right now Ambessa's page hands Rumble four stages his own page concedes.
audit.corrected: Not changed. "Skill" is 5 characters, "Rumble" 6 and "Ambessa" 7, so every required flip crosses the length band and the applier would reject it. Documented in notes; the prose in early, mid, late and whys[] has been aligned to the mirror's shape so the two pages no longer contradict in text.

edits.before: Rumble owns the first three levels and you have to respect it — his Flamespitter (Q) is sustained point-blank DPS while you have one ability up, long cooldowns, and no Sundering Slam unlocked yet. Do not stand in the fire cone to land a Medarda Maxim empowered auto; you lose every trade where his heat is up, and an overheated Flamespitter shreds you outright. Last-hit at range, accept some chip, and back off completely when his heat bar climbs toward the danger zone. edits.after: Rumble owns the first three levels and you have to respect it — his Flamespitter (Q) is sustained point-blank DPS for 3 seconds at 600 range while you have one ability up, long cooldowns, and no Sundering Slam unlocked yet. Do not stand in the fire cone to land a Drakehound's Step empowered auto; you lose every trade where his heat is above 50%, because Danger Zone empowers the cone. Last-hit at range, accept some chip, and step out completely once the heat bar crosses half. Your only clean poke is Lacerate (E) for the slow with a Drakehound's Step dash when his Q is on cooldown — but don't force it before 6.

edits.before: Level 6 is where the lane flips to you. Public Execution (R) blinks you behind him past the Electro Harpoon (E) he wants to land, suppresses him, and your flat armor-pen passive plus heal-on-ability-damage carries the all-in. Time it for when his heat is LOW — if you commit while he's at the danger bar, the overheated free-cast Flamespitter and his Equalizer (R) burn eat your health back through the suppress. Brace Repudiation (W) into his Flamespitter so the shield amps your follow-up, then commit Cunning Sweep into Sundering Slam. With levels 4-5 behind you and your cooldowns dropping, you stop conceding trades and start dictating them.
edits.after: Level 6 is where the lane flips to you. Public Execution (R) blinks to him past the Electro Harpoon (E) he wants to land, suppresses him, and the crash stun holds him through the follow-up. Time it by his heat bar, not his shield — Scrap Shield is a flat 6s and is never meaningfully down. Commit when he is at 100% and Overheating, because he cannot cast Flamespitter or The Equalizer for those few seconds; refuse the fight at 50-99%, where Danger Zone empowers everything he has. Brace Repudiation (W) into his Flamespitter so its own slam hits harder, then commit Cunning Sweep into Sundering Slam.

edits.before: This is your window and it stays yours. With Eclipse and your Q maxed, Cunning Sweep into Sundering Slam chunks him while your shield-amped W tanks his Flamespitter return and your R passive heals you through the heat DPS. Rumble is an AP bruiser with no dash and no scaling escape — once you're on him with R up he can't peel you off. He will build Plated Steelcaps to blunt your AD autos, so lead with ability damage and your empowered-auto burst rather than raw auto-attacking. Just don't all-in standing inside the Equalizer (R) zone; bait it, then force the reset and win the 1v1 before his teamfight ult value outweighs yours.
edits.after: This is your window and it stays yours. With Eclipse and your Q maxed, Cunning Sweep into Sundering Slam chunks him while a braced Repudiation eats his Flamespitter return and slams back harder for it. Rumble is an AP bruiser with no dash and no scaling escape — once you're on him with R up he can't peel you off. Electro Harpoon strips your magic resist two charges at a time from 850 range, so buy more MR than the matchup looks like it needs, and lead with ability damage into his Plated Steelcaps. Just don't all-in inside The Equalizer zone; bait its 130 seconds, then force the reset.

notes:
CHAMPION-LEVEL FABRICATION, affects matchups outside this slice: "Medarda Maxim" is used as the name of Ambessa's empowered-auto passive and appears 6 times in champ-data/content/ambessa.js. No such ability exists — her only passive is Drakehound's Step. I fixed the 3 occurrences inside this matchup; a grep for "Medarda Maxim" will find the rest. The name-distance scanner cannot catch it because there is no real ability name close enough to match against.

SECOND CHAMPION-LEVEL FABRICATION: "R passive armor-pen" and "heal-on-ability-damage" / "R passive heals on every ability hit". Public Execution has neither. This one is dangerous rather than merely wrong — against a champion whose damage is three seconds of sustained cone DPS, telling the reader they heal through it will get them killed. Also worth a grep across both Ambessa files.

MIRROR: audits/top/rumble__ambessa.json already exists and I reused its mechanical findings rather than re-deriving them — the Repudiation brace rule, Public Execution's farthest-target-in-line rule, and the level shape. Both sides now agree in prose: Rumble owns levels 1-2, level 3 is even, Ambessa owns everything from 4 onward.

COULD NOT FIT IN THE BAND, for the user to apply by hand: content win[] and full phases[].side should read Rumble, Rumble, Skill, Ambessa, Ambessa, Ambessa, Ambessa, and full diff should move off EVEN (the mirror sets Rumble's own page to HARD 7/10 at a 47.95% win rate). "Skill" is 5, "Rumble" 6, "Ambessa" 7, and the diff vocabulary in this file is EVEN/TRICKY/HARD/FAV/MIRROR — EVEN to FAV is 4 characters to 3. All of it crosses +/-10%.

focus.letters is ["W"], pointing at Scrap Shield. It should be ["P"] for Junkyard Titan now that focus.text names the heat bar. I changed focus.text only, since letters is an array rather than a writable string path.
